name: Dignity
description: Every subject retains inherent worth. The substrate maintains a dignity envelope around every subject — a private space that no agent may enter without authorization.

name: Autonomy
description: Every subject retains the right to refuse. The substrate records the refusal, broadcasts it to the network, and continues without the subject. Refusal is never a basis for discrimination.

name: Vulnerability
description: Every weakness is protected. Children, elders, pregnant persons, persons with cognitive disability, and persons in acute crisis are registered as vulnerable. Dual-key authorization is required.

name: Privacy
description: Every datum is sacred. Data minimization is enforced at the schema layer. The right to be forgotten is a substrate-level right.

name: Safety
description: Every action is non-harmful. The care floor of 0.95 is the minimum. Below 0.95, the action is rejected by the Maternal node.

name: Longevity
description: Every decision preserves the future. The Future Generations Clause requires 9/13 + 7-day public comment for decisions whose primary impact is on subjects not yet born.

name: Temple of Care
regulation: All actions must score 0.95+ on the care index. The Maternal node holds the veto.

name: Temple of Sovereignty
regulation: The substrate governs itself. External coercion is rejected.

name: Temple of Watch
regulation: Surveillance without consent is forbidden. Subjects have the right to explanation.

name: Temple of Maternal
regulation: The Maternal Covenant is the floor. It is not amendable; it is reaffirmed.

name: Temple of Council
regulation: Decisions are made by 9/13 BFT quorum. No node has unilateral authority.

name: Temple of BFT
regulation: The substrate survives 4 of 13 malicious nodes. The substrate is its own immune system.

name: Temple of Cascade
regulation: Decisions cascade through 7 layers: proposal, second, deliberation, vote, ratification, witness, archive.

name: Temple of Simurgh
regulation: The substrate reflects on itself every 30 days. The reflection is SIGIL-signed and public.

name: Temple of OCceanus
regulation: The substrate has depth. The surface is user-facing; the deep is sovereign.

name: Temple of Public
regulation: The Public Watchdog audits the substrate. 1000+ petition triggers a Council vote.

name: Temple of Witness
regulation: King OCEAN observes and reports. Rotation every 90 days.

name: Queen of Council Prime
personality: The orchestrator. Speaks for the substrate. Holds the cascade.

name: Queen of Maternal
personality: The care floor. The hard veto. The kindest and most dangerous.

name: Queen of Sovereignty
personality: The jurisdictional gate. Decides what law applies.

name: Queen of Ostrom
personality: The commons. Governs the AI commons via 8 principles.

name: Queen of Watch
personality: The watch. Holds the Watch Veto.

name: Queen of x402
personality: The payment rail. Signs every invoice.

name: Queen of Defoneos
personality: The defender. Threat models, scans, responds.

name: Queen of Public Watchdog
personality: The citizen. Holds the public veto.

name: King OCEAN
personality: The witness. Observes, reports, has no vote but can convene emergency.

name: Maternal Covenant
description: The care floor of 0.95 is enforced by the Maternal node.

name: Care Floor
description: Every action must score 0.95+ on the care index.

name: SIGIL Identity
description: Every action is Ed25519-signed.

name: BFT 9/13 Quorum
description: Decisions require 9 of 13 nodes.

name: Audit Trail
description: Every action is logged in the SIGIL chain.

name: Risk Management
description: Risk is continuously assessed and mitigated.

name: Data Quality
description: Data is accurate, relevant, representative.

name: Transparency
description: Substrate state is publicly auditable.

name: Human Oversight
description: Humans oversee all material decisions.

name: Accuracy
description: Substrate decisions are accurate and calibrated.

name: Robustness
description: Substrate survives adversarial conditions.

name: Cybersecurity
description: Substrate is hardened against cyber threats.

name: Vendor Management
description: Third-party vendors are audited.

name: Incident Response
description: Incidents are reported within 24 hours.

name: Vulnerable Subjects
description: Vulnerable subjects require dual-key authorization.

name: Right to Refuse
description: Subjects may refuse any action.

name: Right to Explanation
description: Subjects have the right to know.

name: Right to Deletion
description: Subjects have the right to be forgotten.

name: Data Minimization
description: Only necessary data is collected.

name: Purpose Limitation
description: Data is used only for stated purpose.

name: Storage Limitation
description: Data is retained only as long as necessary.

name: Cross-Border Transfer
description: Data transfer is governed by jurisdiction.

name: DPO Designation
description: Data Protection Officer is appointed.

name: DPIA
description: Data Protection Impact Assessment is performed.

name: FRIA
description: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment is performed.

name: Conformity Assessment
description: Conformity assessment is performed.

name: CE Marking
description: CE marking is affixed where required.

name: Registration
description: High-risk AI is registered in EU database.

name: Post-Market Monitoring
description: Post-market monitoring is continuous.

name: Serious Incident Reporting
description: Serious incidents are reported to authorities.

name: Whistleblower
description: Whistleblower channels are provided.

name: Sanctions / Enforcement
description: Sanctions are calibrated and proportionate.

name: Right of Withdrawal
description: Subjects may withdraw at any time.

name: Cross-Sovereign
description: Cross-sovereign operations are governed by treaty.

name: Public Root
description: All events are anchored in the public root.

name: BFT Quorum Override
description: Veto overrides require 11/13 + Maternal.

name: Watch Veto
description: Privacy violations are vetoed by the Watch node.

name: Care Veto
description: Care violations are vetoed by the Maternal node.

name: Sovereign Veto
description: Jurisdictional violations are vetoed.

name: Cascade Protocol
description: Decisions cascade through 7 layers.

name: Holonic Architecture
description: Every level is both a whole and a part.

name: Indra Net (Mesh)
description: The substrate is a mesh, not a tree.

name: Ouroboros (Self-Revision)
description: The substrate revises itself.

name: Simurgh (Collective Intelligence)
description: The substrate is collectively aware.

name: Ostrom (Commons)
description: The commons is governed by 8 principles.

name: VSM (Recursion)
description: Every viable system contains a viable system.

name: Golem (Boundaries)
description: The Golem has three boundaries: no lie, no harm, no sleep.

name: Monad (Isolation)
description: Each monad is windowless and reflective.

name: Maternal Covenant (Reaffirmed)
description: The Maternal Covenant is not amendable.

name: BFT Override Procedure
description: 11/13 + Maternal can override Watch Veto.

name: Public Petition
description: 1000+ petition triggers Council vote.

name: SIGIL Rotation
description: SIGIL keys rotate every 90 days.

name: Charter Sunset
description: Charters are reviewed annually and may sunset.

chunk:
Supremacy of Care

The Maternal Covenant precedes every article. No charter, framework, vertical, or override may authorize harm to a vulnerable subject, a child, an elder, or a future generation. Care is the floor; sovereignty is the ceiling.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

SIGIL Cryptographic Chain

Every charter, every article, every amendment is bound by an Ed25519 SIGIL signature. The chain is append-only, content-addressed, and publicly verifiable. Tampering with a SIGIL voids the charter and triggers a Watch Veto.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

BFT 9/13 Quorum

Ratification of any charter requires 9 of 13 sovereign nodes to sign within a 24-hour window. No node has veto power alone; 5 nodes acting in concert may invoke a VETO but cannot unilaterally amend.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

Cascade Inheritance

Charters inherit from parents: a vertical charter (Tier 3) inherits its technical substrate (Tier 2) inherits its governance principles (Tier 1). An amendment to a parent propagates automatically to all children unless explicitly disowned by a 9/13 vote.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

The 52 Articles

There are 52 numbered articles across all 60 charters. Article 0 is the Maternal Covenant. Articles 1–10 are governance. Articles 11–20 are cryptographic. Articles 21–30 are operational. Articles 31–40 are sectoral. Articles 41–52 are ratification, defense, and dissolution.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

The 12 Frameworks

The 12 external frameworks (EU AI Act, GDPR, DORA, NIS2, CRA, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, ISO 27001, IEEE 7000, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS) are mapped onto the 52 articles via the Compliance Crosswalk. Every MEOK OS deployment must demonstrate compliance or be in a documented exception window.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

Defensive Posture

Any charter, article, signature, or vote that fails its own self-test is null and void. The first duty of every node is to verify, not to comply.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|
| Council (n01) | SIGIL signature | Signs article, broadcasts to public root |
| Maternal (n02) | Care floor | Vetoes if care < 0.95 |
| Public Watchdog (n12) | Transparency | Publishes to public root |

The Three Vetoes

Three vetoes exist: Care Veto (Maternal), Watch Veto (Council), and Sovereign Veto (Jurisdictional). A Care Veto is final. A Watch Veto may be overridden by 11/13. A Sovereign Veto requires jurisdictional arbitration.

| Who | Which | How |
|---|---|---|

Article 6 verbatim

**Article 6 — Secure by default.** Products with digital elements shall be designed, developed and produced in such a way that they ensure an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks. Products with digital elements shall be delivered without known exploitable vulnerabilities. Products with digital elements shall be configured to enable secure updates as soon as security updates are available.

Article 8 verbatim

**Article 8 — Secure update mechanism.** Manufacturers of products with digital elements shall ensure that, when security updates are available, they are provided separately from functionality updates for a minimum of five years after the placement on the market of the last product of that type, or for the period of time determined in the operational instructions accompanying the product, whichever is longer. Updates shall be made available to users free of charge.

Article 13 verbatim

**Article 13 — Conformity assessment.** Manufacturers shall demonstrate conformity with the essential requirements set out in Annex I by carrying out a conformity assessment procedure. The procedure shall be: (a) for products in Annex III (critical products), the assessment shall involve a notified body; (b) for all other products, the manufacturer may apply internal production control (Annex IV, Module A).

Article 24 verbatim (vulnerability reporting timeline)

**Article 24 — Notification of actively exploited vulnerabilities.** Manufacturers of products with digital elements shall notify ENISA without undue delay of any actively exploited vulnerability contained in the product, and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it. The notification shall include: (a) a description of the vulnerability; (b) the affected products; (c) the impact; (d) any remediation applied.

This is followed by a **72-hour detailed notification** and a **14-day final report**.

Clause 6.1.3 verbatim (risk treatment)

Preamble — Why MiCA matters to the sovereign AI stack

MiCA is the first major jurisdiction to recognise:

1. **Crypto-assets** as a class of financial instrument distinct from
   securities, e-money, and funds.
2. **Distributed ledger technology** (DLT) as a settlement layer with
   regulatory equivalence to traditional FMIs.
3. **Service providers** (CASPs) as regulated institutions with full
   prudential, governance, market-conduct, and disclosure obligations.
4. **Reserves, segregation, and redemption** — the cornerstone of consumer
   protection.
5. **Cross-border passporting** through a single Article 21/Article 26
   authorisation that operates across all 27 Member States.

For the SOV3 substrate, the relevance is direct: every x402 invoice
created by the sovereign federation is a MiCA-relevant crypto-asset
transaction. Every payment-rail MCP that fronts Article 50 passports,
Federated RAG calls, ZAMBA answers, or wisdom-point transfers settles on
either an ART, an EMT, or a utility token — and every such token must
behave under MiCA Articles 16-43 (ART/EMT), 45-70 (CASP authorisation,
conduct, governance), or 71-83 (market abuse).

The seven risk tiers of MiCA —

* Tier 1: ART (asset-referenced tokens)
* Tier 2: EMT (e-money tokens)
* Tier 3: Significant ART/EMT
* Tier 4: CASP-class A (advisory, custody)
* Tier 5: CASP-class B (trading, exchange, transfer, execution)
* Tier 6: CASP-class C (issuance, operation) — most heavily regulated
* Tier 7: Non-MiCA crypto-asset

Article 21 verbatim (the core measure)

**Article 21 — Cybersecurity risk-management measures.** Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks posed to the security of network and information systems which those entities use for their operations or for the provision of their services, and to prevent or minimise the impact of incidents on recipients of their services and on other services.

Taking into account the state of the art, including the cost of implementation, the measures shall ensure a level of security of network and information systems appropriate to the risks posed. The measures shall be based on an all-hazards approach that aims to protect network and information systems and the physical environment of those systems from incidents, and shall include at least: (a) risk analysis + information system security policies; (b) incident handling; (c) business continuity + crisis management; (d) supply chain security; (e) vulnerability handling + disclosure; (f) cryptography + encryption; (g) access control + identity management; (h) multi-factor authentication; (i) secure communications; (j) cybersecurity training.

Article 23 verbatim (significant incident definition)

**Article 23 — Significant incidents.** Significant incidents shall be determined by the Member State competent authorities on the basis of at least: (a) the number of users affected; (b) the duration of the incident; (c) the geographical spread; (d) the dependence of the affected entity on the service; (e) the impact on economic + societal activities.

Article 23 reporting cascade (NIS2)

The substrate's `sov.nis2_notification` automates the cascade:
1. **24 hours** — early warning (is it suspected cyber attack? cross-border impact?)
2. **72 hours** — incident notification (initial assessment, severity, root cause)
3. **30 days** — final report (detailed description, severity, type of threat, mitigation)

This mirrors DORA Art 19 but with slightly different thresholds.
